_comment: drupilot default configuration. Every DRUPILOT_* key can be overridden by an environment variable of the same name (env ALWAYS wins), and a per-project .drupilot.json at the Drupal root overrides these defaults too (env > .drupilot.json > this file). See README, Configuration section.
_php_target_comment: DRUPILOT_PHP_TARGET is the CONSERVATIVE default port floor (8.3, supported on every Drupal 11 branch). It is intentionally distinct from php_support.recommended (8.4), which is the version the /drupilot-setup PHP picker highlights as recommended. Both are valid targets; the default stays at the safe floor while the picker lets the developer move up to 8.4. 8.5 needs Drupal 11.3 or later and has no assumed Rector set (see _php_support_comment).
_soft_deprecations_comment: Policy for SOFT deprecations (scripts/analysis/classify-deprecations.sh). A deprecation is HARD when it is removed in a Drupal major <= the target major (e.g. user_roles(), removed in 11.0.0): Phase 1 always fixes it. It is SOFT when it is removed in a later major (e.g. user_load_by_name(), text_summary(), check_markup(): deprecated in 11.4.0, removed from 13.0.0): it still works on every Drupal 11 core. DRUPILOT_SOFT_DEPRECATIONS: 'report' (default) lists soft ones in the viability and port reports (symbol, deprecated in, removed in, effort) and leaves the code alone; 'defer' records them under 'deferred to Phase 2'; 'fix' fixes them in Phase 1 only when the replacement exists at the declared core floor, through DeprecationHelper::backwardsCompatibleCall() when it exists only on newer cores (e.g. the TextSummary service, 11.4+), and defers them otherwise. Phase 2 (/drupilot-refactor) removes soft ones too, still respecting the floor. A deprecation whose removal version cannot be read is treated as hard (blocking) until reviewed.
_attributes_comment: Optional annotation -> PHP 8 attribute pass (scripts/analysis/convert-attributes.sh, also run-rector.sh --attributes; core types and the core minor each attribute class needs in config/plugin-attributes.json). DRUPILOT_ATTRIBUTES_MODE: 'keep' (default) adds the attribute and keeps the annotation next to it (older cores read the annotation, so the runtime floor is unchanged; static analysis on a core below the attribute's minor reports the class as unknown, so the flow raises core_version_requirement explicitly when it applies the pass) or 'strip' (removes the annotation, only for types whose minor is <= the declared core floor unless --raise-floor). Phase 1 (/drupilot-port) offers it opt-in in keep mode, limited to types available on Drupal 10.3 (--max-since 10.3), raising the floor to e.g. '^10.3 || ^11'; Phase 2 (/drupilot-refactor, 'attributes' scope) runs it in strip mode. DRUPILOT_ATTRIBUTE_PLUGIN_TYPES declares project/contrib plugin types: comma-separated 'Annotation=Fully\Qualified\AttributeClass[@MAJOR.MINOR]' (e.g. 'ExtraFieldDisplay=Drupal\extra_field\Attribute\ExtraFieldDisplay'); a custom type is converted only when its attribute class exists under the Drupal root, and stripped only when a plugin manager references it.
_verify_cores_comment: Core-matrix verification (scripts/analysis/verify-core-matrix.sh). A port that keeps '^10 || ^11' only ever runs on the Drupal 11 test-bed; the matrix also runs PHPStan (phpstan-drupal + deprecation rules, the test-bed's exact versions) and php -l against a cached REFERENCE core per extra leg, built once through `ddev exec composer` in <drupal_root>/.drupilot/cores/ (never the host PHP; its version is frozen in the lockfile under .verify_cores in deterministic mode). A reference leg FAILS on an error the Drupal 11 baseline does not have (an #[\Override] on a method only 11.3+ core declares, a class only Drupal 11 ships); deprecations, missing contrib dependencies (sandbox), findings in tests/, phpstan-drupal advisory rules and runtime-tolerated findings (more arguments than an older core's method takes; the result of a newer core's void method used) never fail a leg. Composer always runs as the container's own binary (never the test-bed's vendor/bin/composer), and a broken phpstan/extension-installer GeneratedConfig.php in the test-bed or a cached reference core is regenerated. php -l also runs on each leg's lowest PHP (its core's PHP minimum or the subject's composer require.php floor, whichever is higher) in a php:X.Y-cli Docker container. DRUPILOT_VERIFY_CORES: 'auto' (default) = the legs the subject's core_version_requirement declares, a lower major also on its floor minor ('^10 || ^11' -> 10.0,10,11; '^10.3 || ^11' -> 10.3,11; '^11' -> nothing extra), 'off' = skip (the Drupal 10 half stays declared-not-verified), or an explicit comma list such as '10,11' or '10.3,11'. A passing Drupal 10 leg makes d10_support 'verified-static' (static only: runtime is not exercised); a blocked network leaves it 'declared-not-verified' and never blocks the port.
_state_comment: Per-subject stage record (state.json in the hidden state dir, written by port-report.sh / run-phpunit.sh through phase_record in common.sh; read by next-step.sh, the post-edit hook and /drupilot-status). Its 'stage' is the highest stage reached (setup < assessed < ported < refactored < tested < contributed) and never goes down. DRUPILOT_STATE_FORCE=true lets a new record lower it (e.g. to restart a port after a refactor); default false.
_want_refactor_comment: DRUPILOT_WANT_REFACTOR: whether the developer opted into the Phase 2 refactor for the next-step ladder (scripts/env/next-step.sh, used by the /drupilot router and /drupilot-status). 'true' makes it recommend /drupilot-refactor right after the port, before the test step, until the subject is refactored; 'false' (default) leaves the refactor opt-in and recommends the tests after the port. It only changes the recommendation, never runs anything.
_workspace_comment: Where the Drupal 11 test-bed is built and how the subject module/theme is placed in it (scripts/env/resolve-workspace.sh + place-subject.sh). When drupilot is pointed at a LOOSE checkout (a module/theme NOT already under a Drupal web/modules/custom), it does NOT scaffold Drupal on top of it (that intermixes the module's files with the Drupal scaffold). Instead it builds Drupal in a sibling directory and places the subject under web/{modules,themes,profiles}/custom/<machine_name>. DRUPILOT_WORKSPACE_DIR: explicit path for that Drupal root (default '' = auto: a sibling '<parent>/<machine_name>-d11'). An already-resolvable Drupal root (the module is already inside one) always wins, so existing layouts are untouched. DRUPILOT_PLACEMENT (move|symlink|copy, default 'move'): move relocates the loose checkout into the test-bed (non-lossy — it stays a git repo, just at a new path); symlink keeps your checkout where it is and links it in (you keep editing your original path; slightly more fragile with ddev-drupal-contrib); copy duplicates it (the original is left untouched). DRUPILOT_ARTIFACTS_DIR: override for the visible, gitignored '.drupilot/' outputs dir (default '' = <root>/.drupilot).
_layers_comment: /drupilot-layers (port a set of modules in dependency order). DRUPILOT_LAYERS_SANDBOX: the test-bed a layer run uses when the set is a LOOSE folder of modules (a set already inside a Drupal root is always ported in place, in that one site): 'per-module' (each module gets its own sibling <name>-d11 workspace, as for a single port) or 'shared' (one workspace, <parent>/<dir>-d11, for the whole set, so a module and the modules it depends on are installed together). Default '' = ask in the command (per-module when autonomous). The command persists the answer to .drupilot.json.
_home_comment: DRUPILOT_HOME: drupilot's hidden data directory: the per-subject machine state (state/<key>/: assess.json, last-test.json, state.json, the determinism lockfile, ...) and the caches (cache/: the drupal-digests checkout, the cached base core). Default '' = $XDG_DATA_HOME/drupilot, i.e. ~/.local/share/drupilot. Read from the environment only (it locates the state before any .drupilot.json can be read); give an absolute path: a leading '~' is expanded, any other relative value is ignored (so is a relative XDG_DATA_HOME), because hooks and scripts run from different directories. Hooks and scripts resolve the same directory: Claude Code's per-plugin data dir is no longer used, and the first command after 0.9.1 that passes its gate copies (never moves) any state 0.9.0 left there. The only new key of the 0.9.x line.
_patterns_comment: Learned-pattern catalog (scripts/analysis/patterns.sh): the pitfalls a port of this project already hit, each with a detector (a POSIX ERE and/or a check-port-safety / scan-signature-changes rule) and the fix. /drupilot-port and /drupilot-refactor scan the subject with it BEFORE changing code and offer to record new patterns at the end; /drupilot-layers shares one catalog across the whole set, so what layer N learned is checked on layer N+1. DRUPILOT_PATTERNS_FILE: the catalog file (default '' = <Drupal root>/.drupilot/patterns.json, the visible self-gitignored artifacts dir; for a module ported by /drupilot-layers, the set's catalog). Point it at a committed file (a relative path is taken from the Drupal root) to share the catalog with a team.
_ddev_timeout_comment: DRUPILOT_DDEV_CREATE_TIMEOUT: wall-clock limit, in seconds, for the 'ddev composer create-project' step of scripts/env/ddev-up.sh (default 900; 0 = no limit). A hung create is stopped with a clear error instead of blocking setup indefinitely. Enforced through 'timeout' (GNU coreutils) or 'gtimeout' (macOS Homebrew coreutils); without either the step runs unbounded.
_core_cache_comment: Cached base core (scripts/env/ddev-up.sh). After a fresh 'composer create-project' (+ Drush), the resulting tree (composer.json/lock, vendor/, the docroot with core, recipes/, scaffold files; never .ddev/, settings*.php or files/) is stored under drupilot's data dir (DRUPILOT_HOME, else $XDG_DATA_HOME/drupilot: cache/core-base/php<PHP>-<core version>/), and a later setup of an EMPTY root copies it in (copy-on-write when the filesystem allows: cp --reflink=auto, cp -c on APFS; else a plain copy), then verifies it with 'ddev composer install' (a failed verification discards the entry and falls back to create-project). DRUPILOT_CORE_CACHE: 'auto' (default) reuses the entry for the core version the lockfile froze for that root, or, when nothing is frozen yet, the newest entry built for the same DRUPILOT_DRUPAL_TARGET that is at most DRUPILOT_CORE_CACHE_MAX_AGE_DAYS old (0 = no limit; the lockfile then freezes that version); 'locked' reuses only the frozen version; 'off' never reuses or stores. DRUPILOT_DETERMINISTIC=false never reuses (it resolves fresh) but still refreshes the cache. DRUPILOT_CORE_CACHE_KEEP: how many entries are kept (newest first). /drupilot-clean --core-cache removes them all. A frozen core version is also honored by a fresh create (drupal/recommended-project:<that version>).
_hooks_comment: Hook behavior toggles. DRUPILOT_POST_EDIT_LINT controls the PostToolUse incremental lint (hooks/scripts/post-edit-lint.sh): 'autofix' (default) runs phpcbf then phpcs and reports when it modified the file; 'report' runs phpcs only (never edits files in place); 'off' disables it. The hook is also phase-aware: during Phase 1 (minimal port) it surfaces compatibility ERRORS only, deferring DrupalPractice style WARNINGS to /drupilot-refactor, and its phpcbf skips the unused-use sniffs (a use added one edit before the code that needs it would be deleted; the validate loop removes truly unused ones). DRUPILOT_SESSION_CONTEXT toggles the SessionStart environment summary (hooks/scripts/session-detect-env.sh): 'on' (default) or 'off'.
_phpcs_ruleset_comment: Which PHPCS ruleset scripts/analysis/run-phpcs.sh (and the post-edit-lint hook, through the resolution run-phpcs.sh records) lints with. DRUPILOT_PHPCS_RULESET: 'auto' (default) uses the subject's OWN ruleset (.phpcs.xml, phpcs.xml, .phpcs.xml.dist or phpcs.xml.dist, in PHPCS's discovery order) found from the subject up to the Drupal root, then up to the subject's git top level, then in the origin checkout of a copy placement; drupilot's own generated phpcs.xml.dist never counts as the project's. Without one, or when PHPCS cannot load it (e.g. it references PHPCompatibility, not installed in the test-bed), it uses Drupal,DrupalPractice and says so. 'drupilot' always uses Drupal,DrupalPractice (the behavior of drupilot 0.8.4 and earlier). Any other value is a ruleset file path (absolute, or relative to the Drupal root). DRUPILOT_PHPCS_TEST_VERSION: the PHPCompatibility testVersion passed with --runtime-set (e.g. '8.1-'). Empty (default) = '<DRUPILOT_PHP_TARGET>-', except that a ruleset's own <config name="testVersion"> is never overridden and a testVersion wrongly declared as a <property> inside a <rule> is passed through. Passing it avoids PHPCompatibility's 'trim(): Passing null' failure when the ruleset leaves the config unset.
_hooks_guard_comment: Guard for repository git hooks (GrumPHP, husky, lefthook, pre-commit, captainhook, core.hooksPath, .git/hooks). drupilot never normalizes skipping them: before a commit the flow runs scripts/contrib/git-hooks.sh, lets the hooks run, and only when a hook cannot complete in the session substitutes its tasks (git-hooks.sh --run-equivalents) and records which validations replaced it in the port report. DRUPILOT_HOOKS_GUARD: 'ask' (default) makes the PreToolUse hook (hooks/scripts/guard-contrib.sh) ask for confirmation before a 'git commit' that skips the hooks (--no-verify, -n, or -c core.hooksPath=...) in a repository where a commit hook is actually installed, in every contribution mode and also in autonomous mode (an unattended run cannot confirm, so it must not skip the hooks); 'off' disables that check. It never denies, and it never changes the push / Merge Request guard.
_deterministic_comment: Reproducibility (DEFAULT ON). When true, drupilot freezes the versions/refs it resolves (Drupal core, the dev toolchain, the digests SHA, DDEV add-ons) into a per-project drupilot-lock.json (under the plugin's state dir, NOT the user's project tree) and reuses them on later runs, so porting the same module twice converges on the same toolchain and result. Set DRUPILOT_DETERMINISTIC=false (the escape hatch) to always resolve fresh (legacy floating behavior) and refresh the lock. This governs only drupilot's own resolution; the Claude Code permission mode still governs Bash/Edit/Write. Helpers: deterministic_mode / lock_get / lock_set / lock_resolve in scripts/lib/common.sh; capture/refresh via scripts/env/lock-sync.sh.
_autonomous_comment: Hands-off mode. When true (or invoked as `/drupilot <subject> auto`), the orchestrator runs setup -> assess -> port -> refactor -> test unattended: no initial confirmation, DRUPILOT_GENERATE_RULES is treated as 'auto' unless explicitly set to 'off', and the local .patch is always written at the end. It NEVER performs outward-facing actions on its own (no git push / Merge Request / contribute) — those stay opt-in via /drupilot-contribute. This only relaxes drupilot's own gates; the Claude Code permission mode still governs Bash/Edit/Write prompts (use acceptEdits or a headless bypass for a fully unattended run).
_issue_comment: Defaults for the Drupal.org issue used when contributing a port (PROMPT 3). The issue itself is created on the web (there is no public issue API, and the GitLab API is blocked by default), so drupilot GENERATES ready-to-paste content + recommended field values via scripts/contrib/make-issue.sh — it does not submit the form. For a Drupal 11 compatibility port the conventional values are DRUPILOT_ISSUE_CATEGORY='Task' and DRUPILOT_ISSUE_PRIORITY='Normal'. DRUPILOT_ISSUE_COMPONENT defaults to 'Code' (every project has it) — verify it against the project's own component list, which is project-specific. DRUPILOT_ISSUE_ASSIGNEE='self' means assign the issue to the account opening it ('unassigned' to leave it open). The Version field is derived from the target base branch (e.g. base 4.0.x -> 4.0.x-dev), not configured here. Non-applicable summary sections (Steps to reproduce, User interface / API / Data model changes) are omitted for a behavior-preserving port.
_core_target_comment: Drupal core compatibility decision (scripts/analysis/core-strategy.sh; helper recommend_core_target). DRUPILOT_CORE_TARGET_STRATEGY: auto (default) | d11-only | keep-d10. 'auto' keeps the widest set ('^10 || ^11') for a backwards-compatible Phase 1 port and switches to '^11' on a BC break / Phase 2 refactor. POLICY: a Drupal 11 port's PHP floor is the resolved DRUPILOT_PHP_TARGET (>= 8.3). Because Drupal 10 itself allows PHP 8.1, keeping D10 declares a composer require.php floor so a D10 + low-PHP site is blocked at install time (composer) instead of fataling at runtime. DRUPILOT_REQUIRE_PHP_FLOOR (default 'detect') sets that floor to the REAL minimum the ported code needs (heuristic scan via scripts/analysis/detect-php-floor.sh, e.g. '>=8.1' when no PHP 8.2/8.3 constructs are used); set it to 'target' to keep the conservative '>=<target>'. The same scan also reports whether the code is compatible with the target at all (php_floor_target_compatible: false when it uses a construct newer than the target). '^11' needs no require.php (core enforces its own minimum). DRUPILOT_KEEP_D10 is a legacy boolean (true -> keep-d10, false -> d11-only), read from the environment or .drupilot.json and honored only while the strategy is 'auto'; an explicit strategy wins.
_requirements_comment: Minimum versions used by preflight.sh. Some carry uncertainty (see PROMPT 1.2): the real gate is functional (e.g. that 'ddev config --project-type=drupal11' works), not just the number. disk_free_min_mb is the free space (MB) /drupilot-doctor's extended check wants on the filesystem of the Drupal root (or the current directory): a test-bed takes a few hundred MB of Composer trees plus a reference core for the core matrix, and the DDEV images several GB more.
_php_support_comment: PHP versions drupilot tunes the Drupal 11 toolchain for. 'supported' = the targets with a Rector PHP set drupilot uses; 'unconfirmed' = a target accepted with a warning, for which no Rector set is assumed (rector_php_set_arg falls back to the highest 'supported' set): 8.5, which Drupal supports from 11.3 on, not on 11.2 or earlier (drupal.org PHP requirements, re-read 2026-10-03). Which core minor runs which PHP is php_supported_for <minor> <php> (yes/no/unknown; unknown is detected at runtime, never assumed).
_digests_comment: Complementary AI-generated Rector rule layer (Dries Buytaert). Git repo, NOT a Composer package. NO LICENSE -> clone into a runtime cache, never vendor/redistribute.
_packages_comment: Composer constraints for the dev toolchain (PROMPT 1.1), installed inside DDEV. These are the verified SUPPORTED RANGES; the EXACT patch versions resolved on first install are frozen per-project in drupilot-lock.json (see _deterministic_comment) and reused while DRUPILOT_DETERMINISTIC is on. extension-installer only autoconfigures phpstan-drupal and upgrade_status only corroborates findings — neither affects the port result, so they carry a broad range and are pinned exactly by the lock rather than here. core_dev (drupal/core-dev: PHPUnit + the Drupal test dependencies, required by run-phpunit.sh) carries NO constraint here on purpose: it must MATCH the installed drupal/core, so the requirement is derived at install time by core_dev_requirement (scripts/lib/common.sh), e.g. drupal/core-dev:~11.4.8. rector (rector/rector) is a transitive dependency of drupal-rector listed here so it is installed with an explicit range and recorded in the lock: palantirnet/drupal-rector 0.21.x (and 1.x up to 1.1.3) throws 'Could not detect twig set.' with rector/rector >= 2.6.2, whose bundled TwigSetList dropped TWIG_24 (verified in DDEV on 2026-10-02: 2.6.1 works, 2.6.2 and 2.6.7 crash). These ranges are only used for a fresh resolve; by default scripts/env/install-toolchain.sh pins the project lock or the shipped known-good set (config/toolchain-reference.json) instead — see _toolchain_comment.
_toolchain_comment: Dev-toolchain installation (scripts/env/install-toolchain.sh). DRUPILOT_TOOLCHAIN_SOURCE picks where each version comes from: 'auto' (default) = in deterministic mode the project lock when it pins the whole known-good set, otherwise the shipped reference config/toolchain-reference.json (exact versions verified together end to end), and the .packages ranges in non-deterministic mode; 'reference' = always the reference set (the repair path after a broken upstream release; the lock is then refreshed); 'range' = the .packages ranges (fresh resolve). Every install ends with a smoke test (a Rector dry-run with the Drupal 10 set + phpstan --version) and exits 3 with the known-good versions when the installed set is broken.
_contrib_comment: URLs and endpoints for the Drupal.org contribution flow (PROMPT 3).
